key_insight: Encoding conditions in the input state lets one shared IQP Born machine represent conditional families beyond the reach of diagonal conditioning at the same qubit count.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables classical training of conditional quantum generative models without condition-dependent diagonal-layer parameters.
method: Encode each condition in the input state and share a single IQP unitary across conditions.
Use efficient reference-state sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation to estimate conditional maximum mean discrepancy and gradients without bias.
Evaluate conditional generation on the Curie–Weiss spin model.
evidence_signal: At 16 qubits, the model captures the magnetization transition at held-out temperatures with sixfold lower mean total variation distance than diagonal conditioning; models up to 2048 qubits reproduce mean squared magnetization away from the crossover.
watch_item: Efficient training requires tractable reference-state sampling and amplitude ratios; the reported results do not establish practical quantum sampling advantage.
paper_title: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines
